title: Generation of knock-in degron tags for endogenous proteins in mice using the dTAG system
protocol: Mix all required pieces for the HDR donor plasmid using Q5 DNA polymerase or an alternative high-fidelity DNA polymerase.
Estimate the annealing temperature for each primer pair using the NEB Tm calculator.
Follow the manufacturer’s guidelines to estimate extension times for PCR amplification.
Amplify 1,000 bp in approximately 20–40 seconds per fragment.
Amplify all DNA fragments.
Run PCR products on a 1.5% agarose gel to isolate the desired amplicon.
Purify isolated amplicons using QIAGEN gel purification kit or similar.
Store purified fragments at −20°C until assembly.
Anneal and phosphorylate sgRNA oligos in a thermocycler at 37°C for 30 min, then 95°C for 5 min, ramping down to 25°C at an interval of 5°C/min.
Linearize and dephosphorylate CRISPR-Cas9 PX459 vector using the QIAGEN miniprep kit.
Digest the linearized plasmid with BbsI.
Prepare the digest mix according to specifications.
Incubate in a thermocycler at 37°C for 40 min.
Incubate in a thermocycler at 65°C for 20 min to deactivate the enzyme.
Add 2 μL Quick CIP to the 50 μL product reaction.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min to dephosphorylate the linearized plasmid.
Run the product on a 1.5% agarose gel.
Cut and gel purify the linearized plasmid band.
Prepare the following mix using the NEB HiFi DNA Assembly Cloning Kit for the HDR donor plasmid reaction, depending on available concentrations (0.05–0.1 pmole/piece).
Incubate the mix in a thermocycler at 50°C for 60 min.
Dilute the annealed sgRNA oligos from step 2: 1 μL in 200 μL ddH2O.
Prepare the ligation mix for PX459 plasmid.
Incubate at room temperature (23°C–25°C) for 15 minutes.
Place on ice.
Transform competent E. coli bacteria with assembled plasmids according to manufacturer’s guidelines.
Use 2 μL of each assembled plasmid per 50 μL of bacteria.
Include a negative assembly mix plate and a negative PX459 ligation control.
Dilute HiFi assembly product 4-fold if using bacteria from another vendor before transforming.
Pick bacterial colonies from positive plates in a sterile field.
Inoculate liquid cultures with appropriate selection antibiotic for each colony.
Purify plasmids using a QIAGEN miniprep kit or equivalent.
Save 1 mL of each culture at 4°C for larger scale prep.
Validate the HDR donor plasmid using restriction enzyme digestion.
Choose 2-3 enzymes that produce 2-3 cuts for a unique gel signature upon digestion.
Validate both plasmids by sequencing.
Inoculate a large culture of one sequence-validated clone per plasmid (100–200 mL).
Purify plasmids using a kit such as the QIAGEN maxiprep kit.
Aim for a concentration of 1–2 μg/μL for each plasmid to be ready for transfection.
Concentrate plasmid DNA using isopropanol precipitation or a kit if the concentration is less than 1 μg/μL.
Mix 0.5 mL of the large culture with 0.5 mL of 50% glycerol in ddH2O (vol/vol) or LB for long-term storage at −80°C if desired.
Store purified and concentrated plasmid DNAs at −20°C until ready to proceed to the cell transfection step.
One day prior to transfection, seed MEFs feeders on one 10-cm tissue culture plate.
Change medium on growing mESCs in culture.
Dissociate 70%–80% confluent mESCs using 0.05% Trypsin.
Quench the Trypsin with medium and dissociate via pipetting to generate a single cell suspension.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated counter.
Centrifuge 2 × 10^6 cells at 350 × g.
Aspirate medium.
Resuspend cells in premixed 100 μL electroporation buffer.
Mix 82 μL Nucleofector Solution with 18 μL Supplement.
Pipette up and down gently until cells are completely resuspended.
Avoid generating air bubbles.
Add the cell suspension to a new tube containing 5 μg PX459 and 5 μg HDR donor plasmids.
Ensure total volume of both plasmids does not exceed 10 μL.
Immediately add the mix to an electroporation cuvette.
Run ES cells program (GC-104) on a Lonza Amaxa 4D Nucleofector.
Gently add 500 μL medium to the cuvette after electroporation.
Avoid pipetting up and down.
Transfer the entire mix gently to a pre-warmed MEF feeders-covered 10-cm dish.
Change medium after 24 h.
Avoid disturbing cells as they recover from electroporation (day 3).
Initiate puromycin selection 48 h after transfection.
Add puromycin to medium at 2 μg/mL before medium change.
Change medium daily for the first 2–3 days of selection to wash off dying cell debris.
Notice expansion of puromycin resistant colonies representing individual clones.
Prepare one flat-bottom 96-well plate with MEF feeders one day in advance.
Aspirate medium from targeting/selection plates.
Wash twice with PBS−/−.
Add 7 mL PBS−/− to the plate and proceed to colony picking.
Pick large colonies with well-defined borders under a stereomicroscope in a sterile laminar flow hood.
Place picked colonies into a prepared Trypsin-containing 96-well plate.
Do not pick colonies that are not singular or too small, and do not include those with differentiation at borders.
Pick clones similar in size for synchronized culture splitting across all wells.
Incubate the 96-well plate containing picked colonies in a 37°C incubator for 10 min.
Shake the plate in the middle of the incubation to help dissociate cells.
Add 75 μl of medium into each well and pipette up and down 10-15 times to gently dissociate colonies into single cells.
Transfer 100 μl of cells from each well to a prepared 96-well plate with MEF feeders containing 75 μl of medium, making the final volume in each well 175 μl.
Return the plates to the incubator.
Change medium every 1-2 days until wells reach 80% confluency (3-5 days).
Dissociate cells with 25 μL Trypsin.
Resuspend in a total of 200 μL medium.
Split into three 96-well plates, 50 μL each, for validation assays.
Prepare gelatin-coated dishes as described in step 9 of "before you begin".
Freeze remaining 50 μL cell suspension by mixing with 50 μL freezing medium (20% DMSO and 80% FBS) to achieve a final concentration of 10% DMSO.
Cover wells with 80 μL mineral oil.
Place in -80°C freezer for short-term storage.
Change medium on analysis plates every 1-2 days from day 7-10.
Optionally freeze at least one additional plate if more downstream analyses are planned.
Take two validation plates when they are 70% confluent.
Treat one plate with 500 nM dTAG-13 or dTAGv-1 in maintenance medium for 2 h.
Fix the treated and control plates in 4% PFA for 10 min.
Perform fluorescent immunostaining on both plates.
Stain both plates using an anti-HA antibody.
Check clones under an epifluorescence microscope.
Take images of clones exhibiting fluorescence signal localized to the subcellular location expected for the target protein in the control plate.
Document absence of signal in the corresponding wells of the treated plate.
Expect a nuclear signal for NELFB.
Perform validation PCR for clones showing HA staining in the expected subcellular compartment (day 4).
Design PCR primers that amplify both wild-type and edited alleles.
Add 40 μl of DNA lysis buffer to each well after washing the plate 3× with PBS+/+.
Incubate overnight (∼16 h) at 55°C in a humidified chamber.
Identify 3–4 heterozygous and homozygous clones from the PCR.
Perform a western blot (day 4–7).
Expand identified clones from the remaining analysis plate into one well in a 24-well plate.
Further expand to two wells in a 12-well plate for immunoblotting analysis.
Treat one of the 12-well plates with 500 nM dTAG-13 or dTAG-v1 for 2 h.
Isolate protein from treated plates.
Perform immunoblotting analysis using anti-HA and antibody against the target protein.
Tagged alleles will express a fusion protein.
Show a size shift corresponding to the molecular weight of FKBP12F36V (∼12 kDa) on the target protein blot.
The HA blot will show higher (two-fold) intensity for homozygous clones.
dTAG treated colonies should show near complete degradation.
Identify correctly targeted clones.
Determine their hetero or homozygosity.
Thaw the frozen clones when ready to proceed to chimeric mouse generation.
Alternatively, proceed with in vitro differentiation experiments if not generating a GEM.
Thaw the clones 7–10 days in advance.
Seed MEFs onto a 12-well plate one day before thawing the clones.
Take out the freezing plate and thaw it in a 37°C incubator for 10-15 minutes.
Once thawed, transfer each clone of interest to one medium-containing well in a 24-well plate with 1 mL of medium.
Change medium daily starting from day 3–7 as needed on feeders.
Dissociate cells into a single cell suspension using Trypsin on the day of injection.
Submit 1–2 clones for injection/aggregation into wild-type embryos.
Once sexually mature, initiate mouse breeding with the highest percentage male chimeric mice.
Cross these males to the desired genetic background to generate a homozygous colony of animals (4 months).
Avoid using female high percentage chimeras if they are karyotypically abnormal or sterile.
Validate homozygosity and heterozygosity of the targeted protein in the colony using immunoblotting.
Screen F1 mice for any morphological or behavioral abnormalities that may reflect unintended phenotypes of the tagged protein.
Ensure an easy and reliable genotyping protocol is in place when establishing a mouse colony.
Dissolve dTAG small molecules in DMSO at a concentration of 1 mg/25 μL.
Aliquot 25 μL per 1.5 mL tube.
Add 475 μL of 10% Cremophor EL in PBS to each aliquot.
Pipette up and down until the solution becomes clear.
Load 500 μL into a 1 mL syringe for injection.
Inject according to animal facility guidelines.
Validate degradation in tissue of interest using an assay such as immunoblotting or immunostaining.
